title: ROS playoff/championship sims run on the OLDEST loaded season (2024), not the newest — sorted(snapshot.seasons, key=luck._season_sort_key) passes objects to a function typed for strings, so every season sorts equal
claimUnderTest: playoff_sim.py:467 `current_season = seasons_sorted[-1]` and the module docstring ('every unplayed regular-season matchup in the current season') claim the sim operates on the newest season. The prior audit attributed the degenerate odds to 'the last loaded season is complete (offseason)'.
observed: `_season_sort_key(season: str) -> int` does `int(season)` inside try/except (TypeError, ValueError). All four ROS call sites hand it a SeasonSnapshot OBJECT, not `s.season`, so int() raises TypeError and the key is 0 for EVERY season. sorted() is then a stable no-op and `[-1]` returns the LAST element of a newest-first list — the OLDEST season. On the live league (seasons 2026, 2025, 2024) the sims resolve current_season = 2024, status 'complete', 8 owners. The whole 2025 season is loaded and ignored. Every other module in the repo (luck.py:193, power.py:79, weekly_recap.py:613) passes `s.season` correctly; only src/ros/ does not.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.public_league.snapshot import build_public_snapshot;from src.api.league_registry import get_default_league;from src.public_league import luck;s=build_public_snapshot(get_default_league().sleeper_league_id, include_nfl_players=False);ss=sorted(s.seasons,key=luck._season_sort_key);print([x.season for x in ss],'-> current:',ss[-1].season, ss[-1].league['status'])"
reproduction.expected: 2026 (or 2025 as the newest season with results)
reproduction.actual: 2024, league status 'complete', 8 of the league's 12 current managers

numericProof.formula: expectedWins[o] == wins_2024[o] for all 8 owners (schedule is empty, so sim_wins never increments past the seeded record)

userImpact: Every number on /league -> Championship and /league -> Trade Deadline is a replay of a regular season that ended ~20 months ago. A manager reads '100.0% playoff odds' or '42.6% championship odds' as a forward-looking estimate for 2026 and buys or sells on it. The bug is not confined to the offseason: mid-2026 the sims would still be simulating 2024.

priorFinding.note: Confirms the degenerate output (playoffOdds in {0,1}, one-hot seedDistribution, integer expectedWins, worstPlayoffOddsSe 0.0) but REFUTES the stated root cause. It is not 'the last loaded season is complete'; the sim is not reading the last season at all. 2025 is loaded and skipped. One-line fix at 4 sites: key=lambda s: luck._season_sort_key(s.season).

whatWorks: Once a season is chosen, the seeding, tiebreak-by-PF and bracket code all execute; the arithmetic downstream of the wrong season is internally consistent.
rootCause: Type mismatch between `_season_sort_key(season: str)` and the SeasonSnapshot objects the four ROS call sites pass it, silently swallowed by `except (TypeError, ValueError): return 0`.
requiredRepair: Change `key=luck._season_sort_key` to `key=lambda s: luck._season_sort_key(s.season)` at src/ros/playoff_sim.py:464,546,562 and src/ros/power_v2.py:325. Then add an explicit preseason guard so a season with zero scored games returns honestly-unknown odds instead of falling back to a completed season.
dependencies: W17-F002 (the Seller mislabel) is downstream of this and of the missing-owner coercion.

title: The #1 ROS-strength team is told 'Seller — sell aging win-now players' on /league -> Trade Deadline because he is absent from the 2024 sim and absence is coerced to 0.0 playoff odds
claimUnderTest: trade_deadline.py:61-63 — 'When a map is empty (e.g. no cached sim yet), the missing dimension defaults to 0 — the classifier degrades cleanly.'
observed: `po = float((playoffs.get(owner) or {}).get('playoffOdds') or 0.0)` cannot distinguish 'this owner missed the playoffs' from 'this owner was not in the simulated season'. Four of the league's 12 managers (Brent, Blaine, Kich, jstuedle) joined after 2024 and are absent from the sim; they receive a confident 0.0. `classify_team` reads only playoff odds, championship odds and roster age — it NEVER reads `team_ros_strength_percentile` for the label — so Brent, ranked 1 of 12 with the strongest roster in the league (teamRosStrength 645.12, strength percentile 100%), is rendered as 'Seller'. Collin (percentile 75%, 3rd strongest) is also 'Seller'. Roy (percentile 25%, 3rd weakest) is 'Hold / Evaluate' because he made the 2024 playoffs. Confirmed in the rendered DOM, not just the payload.

reproduction.command: timeout 400 .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W17/page-render-probe.py  # loads /league?tab=rosTradeDeadline through Playwright request interception per AUDIT_PROTOCOL
reproduction.expected: the strongest roster in the league is not told to sell
reproduction.actual: rendered row: 'Brent  0.0%  0.0%  100.0%  Seller  Sell aging win-now players. Prioritize 2026/2027 picks and 23-or-younger upside.'

numericProof.formula: label = classify_team(playoff_odds_pct=0.0, championship_odds_pct=0.0, strength_pct=1.0) -> falls through every buyer band to 'Seller'; strength_pct is accepted as an argument and never consulted for the label

userImpact: A manager holding the best rest-of-season roster in the league is instructed, on a page he can reach in two clicks, to trade away his win-now players for picks. Four of twelve managers get an inverted recommendation with no warning that the underlying sim does not know they exist.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced against live data AND in the rendered DOM (the prior finding executed build_team_directions() only). Adds: classify_team accepts team_ros_strength_percentile and never uses it for the label, which is why a 100th-percentile roster cannot rescue itself from a 0.0 odds input.

whatWorks: The 8 owners who DO appear in the sim get labels that are internally consistent with the (wrong-season) odds they were fed.
rootCause: `or 0.0` collapses None/absent to a confident zero, and the classifier's band ladder has no branch that consults roster strength.
requiredRepair: Distinguish absent from zero: return None and render 'no read' for owners the sim did not cover. Separately, make strength percentile a real term in classify_team or stop accepting it.

title: CARDINAL RULE HOLDS: no ROS value reaches rankDerivedValue, the trade calculator, or the rankings board — verified in both directions at runtime
claimUnderTest: src/ros/__init__.py — 'HARD-isolated from dynasty rankings and trade-calculator math — ROS values must never re-rank dynasty players, change trade values, or modify market values.'
observed: Three independent checks all pass. (1) Key scan of the live `/api/data?view=app` contract for any key matching ^(ros[A-Z]|ros_|restOfSeason|teamRos): ZERO hits at any depth. (2) `src/api/data_contract.py`, `src/trade/*.py` and `src/canonical/*.py` contain no import of `src.ros` (grep returns nothing). (3) Every write path under `src/ros/` resolves through `ROS_DATA_DIR = <repo>/data/ros`; the only writes outside it are none. The reverse coupling is real but benign: `src/ros/lineup.py` is imported by `src/roster_intel/`, `src/league_intel/replacement.py` and `src/api/gameplan.py` — that is the shared LINEUP OPTIMIZER (a pure function of slots + weights), not a ROS value, and `src/api/gameplan.py:244` explicitly documents 'NEVER mixed with rosValue'.

reproduction.expected: zero ROS-prefixed keys in the contract; zero src.ros imports in the value pipeline

numericProof.formula: count(keys matching ^(ros[A-Z]|ros_|restOfSeason|teamRos)) + count(src.ros imports in data_contract/trade/canonical)

userImpact: None — this is the invariant holding. Recorded so a future change that breaks it has a baseline.

priorFinding.note: The prior ROS area has no isolation finding. This is the user's cardinal rule and it holds.

claimUnderTest: Workstream hypothesis: data/ros/aggregate/latest.json may be months stale and presented as current.

title: HANDOFF.md verified: the 6 duplicate aggregate rows and 16 non-lowercase canonicalNames are still present exactly; the '40 of 666 unmatched' figure is stale — it is now 30 of 666
claimUnderTest: HANDOFF.md:138-140 — 'data/ros/aggregate/latest.json has 6 duplicate player rows (the same player under two naming conventions) and 16 rows with non-lowercase canonicalName; 40 of 666 rostered players fail to match.'
observed: Duplicates: CONFIRMED, exactly 6 groups / 6 extra rows, all casing-only collisions after normalize_player_name (nate landman, cam skattebo, cam ward, tank dell, cam bynum, mitch tinsley). Non-lowercase: CONFIRMED, exactly 16 rows. Unmatched: SUPERSEDED — 30 of 666, not 40, because the resolve_canonical_name join fix documented in team_strength.py:69-97 landed. The duplicate rows are worse than a cosmetic count: the join in team_strength.py uses `by_name.setdefault`, and the aggregate list is ordered by rosValue descending, so it always keeps the HIGHER-valued row and discards the better-supported one. Cam Ward: 33.12 (sourceCount 1) kept, 21.18 (sourceCount 3) discarded. 5 of the 6 duplicated players are rostered, on 5 different teams (Brent/nate landman, Eric/cam ward, Ty/cam bynum, Kich/tank dell, jstuedle/cam skattebo), each inflating that team's starting-lineup score.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.utils.name_clean import normalize_player_name;import collections;p=json.load(open('data/ros/aggregate/latest.json'))['players'];c=collections.Counter(normalize_player_name(x['canonicalName']) for x in p);print('dups',sum(v-1 for v in c.values() if v>1));print('nonlower',sum(1 for x in p if x['canonicalName']!=x['canonicalName'].lower()))"

numericProof.formula: value_used = first row in rosValue-desc order == max(candidates); correct value = 4-source blend of all observations

userImpact: The ROS Strength table on /league overstates five teams by the difference between a 1-source outlier and the multi-source consensus for one player each. The Pick Projector's reverse-standings order is derived from the same composite.

priorFinding.note: F12 is about DISTINCT players colliding onto one name (byron murphy, byron young) — the opposite failure. This is ONE player splitting into two rows on casing, plus the confirmation/refutation of the two HANDOFF.md counts. Both defects live in the same identity layer.

whatWorks: The read-side join fix (resolve_canonical_name on both sides) is real and cut unmatched from 40 to 30.
rootCause: src/ros/aggregate.py copies each parser's canonical_name verbatim instead of normalizing, so casing variants key as distinct players. team_strength.py:92-97 deliberately declines to fix the writer because canonicalName doubles as a display fallback.
requiredRepair: Give the aggregate a normalized join key alongside a display name, and merge on the key. HANDOFF.md's '40 of 666' should be corrected to 30.

title: Best-ball lineup optimizer is EXACT, not greedy-correct-by-accident: 360 randomized brute-force trials including non-laminar slot sets, zero deviations; all 12 live lineups legal
claimUnderTest: ADR-007 (docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md) says the fill was 'greedy-correct-by-accident' — optimal only while slot eligibility is laminar.
observed: SUPERSEDED. The greedy was replaced by weight-descending matroid greedy with augmenting paths (Kuhn) at lineup.py:224-275. I wrote my own brute force (exhaustive DFS over slots, independent of the repo's tests) and ran 360 randomized rosters across 3 slot sets — the live 21-slot league set, a non-laminar WR/TE + FLEX + SUPER_FLEX set, and a two-family IDP_FLEX-beside-dedicated-DL/LB/DB set — with hybrid fantasy_positions, injuries and byes. Zero score deviations, zero legality violations. Separately validated the 12 LIVE lineups served by /api/ros/team-strength: no player started twice, every player eligible for its slot under fantasy_positions, and the slot multiset matches the registry's starters exactly (QB1/RB2/WR3/TE2/FLEX2/SFLEX1/K1/DL3/LB3/DB3) for all 12 teams. The 0.72/0.18/0.05/0.05 composite also reproduces to the cent on all 12.
userImpact: None — the lineup math is sound. Users can trust the starters shown on the ROS Strength expandable.

priorFinding.note: Supersedes ADR-007's characterisation. No prior-index finding covers optimizer exactness; the prior ROS area does not challenge it.

whatWorks: solve_optimal_assignment, _canonicalize_slots, _player_eligible_for_slot over fantasy_positions, and the composite arithmetic.

title: Weekly DISTRIBUTIONS are modelled (per-player Gaussian draws with the exact lineup re-solved on each draw), but the season sim then collapses each team to a symmetric Gaussian, discarding the right skew best ball creates
claimUnderTest: Workstream question: are weekly distributions modelled, or only mean totals? Best ball is a max-of-distribution product; using means understates it.
observed: Distributions ARE modelled at the player level. The best-ball presim (BEST_BALL_PRESIM_MIN_WEEKS 120 to MAX 1200, adaptive to a 1% relative SE on the mean) draws each player's weekly score from Gaussian(rosValue-derived mean, mean x per-position CV), solves the EXACT optimal lineup on every draw, and takes the empirical (mean, sd) of the resulting team total. That correctly captures the max-of-distribution lift in the FIRST TWO MOMENTS. It is then thrown away: `_simulate_matchup` (championship.py:150-152) and the regular-season loop both draw `rng.gauss(dist.mean, dist.sd)`, a SYMMETRIC distribution. A best-ball team total is right-skewed by construction (it is a maximum over an eligibility structure); modelling it as Gaussian understates the upper tail, which is exactly the region that decides single-elimination brackets. The payload's `bestBallVarianceBump: 1.1` plus a depth-proportional lift is a scalar patch on sd, not a shape correction.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/rosPlayoffOdds | python3 -c "import json,sys;print({k:v for k,v in json.load(sys.stdin)['data'].items() if k!='playoffOdds'})"
reproduction.expected: a distribution family that can be right-skewed
reproduction.actual: {'bestBallVarianceBump': 1.1, 'bestBallVarianceMode': 'depth_aware', 'pointsModelSource': 'fallback-constants'} — sd scaling only; sampling is rng.gauss

numericProof.formula: team weekly score ~ N(mu, sigma) vs the true max-over-eligible-assignments distribution, which has positive skew

userImpact: Championship odds for high-variance, deep-bench teams are understated and for low-variance teams overstated, by an amount nobody has measured. It is a second-order error today, dominated by W17-F001.

priorFinding.note: F24 calls _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION dead code with a docstring divisor mismatch. My finding is about the SHAPE the presim's output is collapsed into, which is orthogonal and survives regardless of which CV table is live.

whatWorks: The presim itself: adaptive draw count, exact lineup per draw, empirical mean+sd. That is a genuinely good best-ball model for two moments.
rootCause: The presim's empirical sample is summarised to (mean, sd) and discarded instead of being retained and resampled.
requiredRepair: Keep the presim's empirical team-score sample and resample from it (bootstrap) in the season and bracket loops instead of rng.gauss.

title: playoff_sim stamps converged: true on a payload whose headline number is not the one it tested — the SE criterion covers playoff odds only, and championship odds still move 2.25 percentage points run-to-run at the shipped sim count
claimUnderTest: playoff_sim.py:78-90 — 'Simulation counts are now CONVERGENCE-DRIVEN: a fixed count is either wasteful or wrong, and it cannot tell you which, because it reports no error bar.'
observed: Two distinct problems. (1) `worst_se = max(_proportion_se(playoff_count[o]/completed, completed))` tests PLAYOFF odds only. Because the regular-season schedule is empty (W17-F001) playoff odds are deterministic, so worstPlayoffOddsSe is exactly 0.0 and the loop halts at MIN_SIMULATIONS=2000 while stamping `converged: true` — on a payload that also carries championshipOdds, which are NOT converged at 2000 (the file's own championshipOddsCi for Joey is [0.3812, 0.4242], +/-2.15pp). (2) championship.py has no adaptive loop at all: fixed n_simulations=10000, and its payload exposes no CI and no convergence field, so the surface the UI actually reads publishes a bare point estimate. I ran simulate_championship_odds 10 times with independent RNG: Joey mean 0.4247, sd 0.0066, min 0.4153, max 0.4378 — a 2.25pp spread on the number rendered as '42.6%'.

reproduction.expected: a stated uncertainty on the rendered championship odds
reproduction.actual: no CI, no convergence field; measured run-to-run sd 0.66pp and spread 2.25pp

numericProof.formula: spread_pp = (max - min) * 100 over 10 independent runs at the shipped n

userImpact: Two managers refreshing on either side of a scheduled rebuild can see 41.5% and 43.8% for the same team with nothing on the page indicating that is noise. The `converged: true` flag actively misleads anyone auditing the payload.

priorFinding.note: F09 is about the two engines DISAGREEING (I confirm: 0.4025 in latest_playoff.json vs 0.4263 in latest_championship.json for Joey, 2.4pp apart). This adds the measured run-to-run variance of the one the UI reads, and the separate defect that playoff_sim's `converged` flag certifies a quantity that is not the one at risk.

whatWorks: playoff_sim's adaptive loop and its per-team CIs are real machinery; they are simply pointed at the wrong statistic and short-circuited by the degenerate schedule.
rootCause: Convergence criterion scoped to one output of a multi-output sim; championship.py never got the adaptive loop at all.
requiredRepair: Include championship-odds SE in the stopping rule; give championship.py the same adaptive loop and emit CIs; render the interval.
dependencies: W17-F001 (the zero SE is a symptom of the empty schedule)

title: The 72/18/5/5 team-strength formula is still live, hardcoded, never validated — and its labelled weights are not its actual contributions: coverage and health are stamped 5% each and move the composite by 0.46 and 0.24 points on a 298-point spread
claimUnderTest: The /league ROS Strength tab renders the sentence '72% starting lineup + 18% best-ball depth + 5% positional coverage + 5% health' directly to the user.
observed: The constants are unchanged and hardcoded (the 'can be overridden per-league via settings later' comment is still a TODO). They are coefficients on incommensurable quantities: startingLineupScore is an unbounded sum over 21 slots (live range 446-829), benchDepthScore an unbounded sum over 8 (67-211), while coverage and health are bounded 0-100. Measured on the 12 live teams: starting contributes 93.64% of the mean composite with sd 75.2, depth 4.24% with sd 7.05, coverage 1.04% with sd 0.129, health 1.07% with sd 0.066. Against a composite spread of 298.54 points, coverage moves 0.46 and health 0.24. The two terms the UI advertises as 10% of the answer jointly account for 0.23% of the discrimination between teams. Note this is a scale problem, not a weight problem — power_v2.py does the same kind of blend correctly by converting every input to a percentile first.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,statistics;ts=json.load(open('data/ros/team_strength/latest.json'));t={'starting':[0.72*x['startingLineupScore'] for x in ts],'depth':[0.18*x['benchDepthScore'] for x in ts],'coverage':[0.05*x['positionalCoverageScore'] for x in ts],'health':[0.05*x['healthAvailabilityScore'] for x in ts]};[print(k,round(statistics.pstdev(v),3),round(max(v)-min(v),3)) for k,v in t.items()]"
reproduction.expected: term spreads roughly in the ratio 72:18:5:5

userImpact: A manager reading 'positional coverage is 5% of this score' will believe improving bench coverage moves his ROS rank. It cannot — the term's entire dynamic range across the league is under half a point.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced on today's snapshot with a different statistic (per-term standard deviation and spread across the 12 teams, rather than a single team's percentage split). Also confirms PRIOR-A19-F07: grep finds no backtest, calibration or holdout for any of these four constants; tests/ros/test_team_strength.py re-implements the same formula and asserts equality with itself.

whatWorks: The arithmetic is exact — I reproduced teamRosStrength to the cent for all 12 teams. Positional coverage now does discriminate (90.87-100 rather than a constant 100), so the LI-5 slot-derived rewrite worked; it just cannot matter at this weight and scale.
rootCause: Weighted sum over quantities with different units and ranges, presented to users as a percentage decomposition.
requiredRepair: Percentile-normalise the four components before weighting (as power_v2.py already does), or stop describing them as percentages in the UI copy.

title: direction.py's position-aware veteran-age table is unreachable in production — build_section never passes teams, so ageProfile is {} on all 12 live rows and the age-gated Strong Seller branch can never fire
claimUnderTest: direction.py:1-16 — the classifier 'Combines ... Roster age profile (computed from the live player pool)', with a spec-verbatim per-position veteran table (QB 32+, RB 26+, WR 29+, TE 30+, DL/EDGE 30+, LB 29+, DB 29+). The rendered page says direction is 'based on ROS playoff + championship odds + team strength + roster age.'
observed: `build_section(snapshot)` does `_ = snapshot` and calls `build_team_directions()` with no `teams` argument. `build_team_directions` then evaluates `roster_age = build_roster_age_profile(...) if team_obj else {}` where team_obj is always None, so `age_heavy = bool({}.get('vetCount', 0) >= 4)` is always False. All 12 rows in the live payload carry `ageProfile: {}`. The 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' band, which the docstring gates on 'AND age-heavy roster', is therefore structurally unreachable on the live path, and the page's own description of its inputs is false.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/rosTradeDeadline | python3 -c "import json,sys;t=json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['teams'];print('empty ageProfile:',sum(1 for r in t if not r.get('ageProfile')),'of',len(t))"

userImpact: An older win-now roster and a young one get identical direction labels, and the page tells the user roster age was considered.

priorFinding.note: F28 is about the documented band table not matching the fallthrough order — a different defect in the same file. The age input being wholly absent from the live call is not in the prior set.

whatWorks: _is_veteran and build_roster_age_profile are correct in isolation and are exercised by unit tests; nothing calls them from the serving path.
rootCause: build_section discards the snapshot it is handed instead of threading rosters through to build_team_directions.
requiredRepair: Thread the Sleeper overlay's teams (with ages) into build_team_directions, or delete the age branch and correct the page copy.

title: Playoff field size ignores the league: championship._simulate_bracket hardcodes a literal 6 while the live 2026 league is a 7-team playoff, and the same function's caller counts 'made the playoffs' with a different constant
claimUnderTest: championship.py:9-11 — 'Single-elimination 6-team bracket (2 byes + 4 wild-card matchups in round 1 ...). Configurable per league.'
observed: Not configurable, and internally inconsistent. `simulate_championship_odds(playoff_seeds=6, bye_seeds=2)` are plain defaults and no caller ever overrides them — scrape.py:368/372 pass only `best_ball`, and neither module reads the league's Sleeper settings. The live 2026 league's own settings say `playoff_teams: 7` (the 2024 league it is actually simulating said 5); the rendered page states '6 playoff seeds · 2 byes' for both. Worse, `_simulate_bracket` does not even use its own module's parameter: line 80 computes the field with a hardcoded literal — `len([s for s in seeded_owners if seeded_owners.index(s) < 6]) or 6` — while line 239 counts a team as having made the playoffs when `finish <= playoff_seeds`. If anyone ever passed playoff_seeds=7 the bracket would still seat 6 and the playoff-odds count would credit 7.

reproduction.actual: 6, with the field size hardcoded to a literal 6 at championship.py:80

userImpact: Championship and playoff odds are computed for a bracket the league does not play. The 7th seed's real path to a title is priced at zero.

priorFinding.note: Confirms 'hardcoded to 6/2 for every league' and adds the specific live mismatch (2026 league is playoff_teams 7) plus the internal inconsistency between championship.py:80's literal and :239's use of the parameter.

whatWorks: bye_seeds IS threaded correctly into the bracket (line 96-97); only the field size is hardcoded.
requiredRepair: Derive playoff_seeds/bye_seeds from the current season's Sleeper settings and pass them through scrape.py; replace the literal 6 at championship.py:80 with the parameter.

title: Not one ROS source supplies a point projection — all 1,285 rows across the five live CSVs have an empty projection column, yet draftSharksRosSf is registered is_projection_source: True
claimUnderTest: src/ros/sources/__init__.py:24 — 'is_projection_source bool — true if source provides per-player point projections', set True for draftSharksRosSf (the highest-weighted source, 1.25).
observed: Every one of the five live source CSVs carries a `projection` column and every row of it is empty: draftSharksRosSf 0/939, fantasyProsRosOverall 0/389, fantasyProsRosSf 0/538, ffc2qbAdp 0/200, fantasyProsRosIdp 0/219. The entire ROS board is therefore a rank blend converted to a 0-100 index by rank_to_score, with no forward-looking point estimate anywhere. That is consistent with src/api/gameplan.py:36-52, which warns downstream consumers that rosValue 'is not points, despite the arithmetic downstream of it' — but the registry flag says the opposite, and it is the flag a reader checks. Two of the five sources are additionally registered source_type 'dynasty_proxy' with is_ros: False (fantasyProsRosSf w0.85, fantasyProsRosIdp w1.05), i.e. multi-year dynasty rankings feeding a rest-of-season product.

reproduction.command: for f in data/ros/sources/*.csv; do .venv/bin/python -c "import csv,sys;r=list(csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[1])));print(sys.argv[1], len(r), sum(1 for x in r if (x.get('projection') or '').strip()))" $f; done
reproduction.actual: draftSharksRosSf: 939 rows, 0 with projections (same for all five)

numericProof.formula: sum(rows with non-empty projection) across all registered sources

userImpact: Anyone reading the registry or /api/ros/sources believes the board is projection-backed. It is a rank consensus, and 2 of 5 inputs are dynasty (multi-year) rankings rather than rest-of-season ones. The 'rest-of-season' label on every ROS surface overstates the horizon fidelity of the data.

priorFinding.note: F11 says the board is 23-41% multi-year dynasty rankings with no horizon disclosure — confirmed (2 of 5 sources are source_type dynasty_proxy, is_ros False). This adds the separate, sharper fact that the projection column is empty in 100% of rows across ALL five sources while one of them advertises is_projection_source: True.

whatWorks: The rank-to-score path itself runs and produces a coherent 0-100 index; the honesty problem is in the metadata, not the arithmetic.
rootCause: The flag was declared for a fetcher capability that was never delivered; the CSV schema reserves the column and nothing fills it.
requiredRepair: Set is_projection_source False until a projection feed exists, and surface the dynasty-proxy share on /tools/ros-data-health.

title: data/ros/aggregate/history is 857 MB and 796 files tracked in git against a documented 'rolling 30-day archive' — there is no prune code anywhere and the oldest snapshot is 98 days old
observed: 796 files spanning 2026-04-28 to 2026-08-04 (98 days), 857 MB, all tracked (git ls-files data/ros/aggregate/history returns 796). Plus 4,653 tracked run files under data/ros/runs. Total 5,463 tracked files under data/ros. scrape.py:615-616 writes a new ~1.1 MB archive on every run (roughly every 3 hours) and no prune, cleanup or unlink exists anywhere under src/ros/ or scripts/. The word 'rolling' has no implementation.

reproduction.command: ls data/ros/aggregate/history | wc -l; du -sh data/ros/aggregate/history; git ls-files data/ros/ | wc -l; grep -rn 'prune\|unlink\|cleanup' src/ros/
reproduction.expected: ~240 files (30 days at 8/day), grep finds a prune
reproduction.actual: 796 files, 857 MB, 5463 tracked; grep finds nothing

userImpact: Indirect: clone and CI checkout time, and every ROS refresh commit carries another megabyte into history permanently.

priorFinding.note: Re-measured on today's tree: 796 snapshots (prior said 792) and 4,653 run files (prior said 4,633), 857 MB for history alone. Growth of ~4 snapshots and ~20 run files since the prior audit confirms the mechanism is still running unbounded.

whatWorks: The archive write itself is correct and the files are readable.
rootCause: No retention implementation was ever written for a documented retention policy.
requiredRepair: Add a prune to scrape.py's aggregate write (keep N days), and stop force-adding history to git.
